topics.name: Topic 1 Global Hazards
points: 1.1a Why do we have weather extremes? Global circulation, pressure belts and climate zones
1.1a Distribution and causes of tropical storms and El Niño/La Niña-related drought
1.1b When does extreme weather become a hazard? UK weather hazard case study: causes, consequences, responses
1.1b Non-UK weather hazard case study (flash flooding/tropical storm or heat wave/drought): causes, consequences, responses
1.2a What processes occur at plate boundaries? Earth's structure, slab pull and ridge push
1.2a Constructive, destructive, conservative and collision boundaries, hotspots; earthquakes and shield/composite volcanoes
1.2b How can tectonic movement be hazardous? Tectonic event case study: causes, consequences, responses
1.2c How does technology have the potential to save lives in hazard zones? Building design, prediction, early warning

topics.name: Topic 2 Changing Climate
points: 2.1a What evidence is there for climate change? Quaternary to present; sea ice, ice cores, temperature data, paintings, diaries
2.1b Is climate change a natural process? Sunspots, volcanic eruptions, Milankovitch cycles
2.1b The natural greenhouse effect and the enhanced greenhouse effect
2.1c Why is climate change a global issue? Worldwide social, economic and environmental impacts in the 21st century
2.1c UK impacts of 21st-century climate change: weather patterns, seasons, industry

topics.name: Topic 3 Distinctive Landscapes
points: 3.1a What is a landscape? Built and natural landscapes
3.1b Where are the physical landscapes of the UK? Upland, lowland and glaciated landscapes and their distinctive characteristics
3.2a Geomorphic processes: weathering, mass movement, erosion, transport and deposition
3.2a Coastal landforms: headlands, bays, caves, arches, stacks, beaches and spits
3.2a River landforms: waterfalls, gorges, V-shaped valleys, floodplains, levees, meanders and ox-bow lakes
3.2b UK coastal landscape case study: landforms, processes, geology and climate, human activity and management
3.2b UK river basin landscape case study: landforms, processes, geology and climate, human activity and management

topics.name: Topic 4 Sustaining Ecosystems
points: 4.1a What are ecosystems? Interdependence; global distribution, climate, flora and fauna of major ecosystems
4.2a Biodiversity in tropical rainforests: climate, nutrient cycle, soil profile, water cycle, interdependence
4.2b Why tropical rainforests are exploited: goods and services; logging, mineral extraction, agriculture, tourism
4.2b Case study of a sustainable management attempt in a tropical rainforest
4.3a What is it like in Antarctica and the Arctic? Climate, land and sea features, flora and fauna; interdependence
4.3a Impacts of human activity on one polar region
4.3b Small-scale case study of sustainable management in one polar region
4.3b Global-scale case study of management in one polar region (e.g. Antarctic Treaty)

topics.name: Physical geography fieldwork (Paper 1 Section B)
points: Questions fieldwork can investigate and appropriate enquiry processes in a physical context
Fieldwork techniques and methods, including observation and measurement
Processing and presenting fieldwork data (maps, graphs, diagrams)
Analysing and explaining field data using case studies and theories
Drawing evidenced conclusions from fieldwork data
Critically reflecting on data, methods, conclusions and knowledge gained

topics.name: Topic 5 Urban Futures
points: 5.1a Changing global pattern of urbanisation; world cities and megacities since 1950
5.1b Causes of rapid urbanisation in LIDCs: rural-urban migration and internal growth
5.1b Consequences of rapid urban growth in LIDCs
5.1b Suburbanisation, counter-urbanisation and re-urbanisation in ACs
5.2a AC city case study: location, migration, ways of life and contemporary challenges
5.2a LIDC or EDC city case study: location, migration, ways of life; informal settlements, informal jobs, health, waste
5.2b How can cities become more sustainable? One sustainability initiative for each city

topics.name: Topic 6 Dynamic Development
points: 6.1a What is development? AC, EDC, LIDC classification and global distribution
6.1a Measuring development: GNI per capita, HDI and other economic and social measures
6.1b Human and physical factors causing uneven development
6.1b Debt, trade and political unrest making it hard to escape poverty
6.2a LIDC case study: development so far, Rostow's model and Sustainable Development Goals
6.2a LIDC case study: political, social and environmental context
6.2b LIDC case study: international trade, TNC investment and international aid
6.2c LIDC case study: one top-down and one bottom-up development strategy

topics.name: Topic 7 UK in the 21st Century
points: 7.1a UK human and physical characteristics; water stress and housing shortages
7.1b UK population trends since 2001 and the Demographic Transition Model
7.1b Ageing population: causes, effects, distribution and responses
7.1b Changing population structure and ethnic diversity in a named UK place
7.1c Major UK economic changes since 2001
7.1c Core UK economic hubs; changes in one economic hub
7.2a The UK's political role in one global conflict and international organisations
7.2b The UK's cultural influence: media exports
7.2b Contribution of ethnic groups to UK cultural life (food, media or fashion)

topics.name: Topic 8 Resource Reliance
points: 8.1a Why demand for food, energy and water outstrips supply
8.1a Human modification of environments to obtain resources (farming, fishing, deforestation, mining, reservoirs, water transfer)
8.2a Food security and the human and physical factors influencing it
8.2a Global patterns of food access (World Hunger Index, calorie consumption)
8.2a Malthusian and Boserupian theories
8.2b Case study of one country's attempts to achieve food security (local and national scale)
8.2c Sustainability of food security strategies: ethical consumerism, food production, technology, bottom-up approaches

topics.name: Human geography fieldwork (Paper 2 Section B)
points: Questions fieldwork can investigate and appropriate enquiry processes in a human context
Fieldwork techniques and methods, including observation and measurement
Processing and presenting fieldwork data (maps, graphs, diagrams)
Analysing and explaining field data using case studies and theories
Drawing evidenced conclusions from fieldwork data
Critically reflecting on data, methods, conclusions and knowledge gained

topics.name: Geographical Exploration (synoptic, decision-making exercise)
points: Synoptic paper drawing on Topics 1 to 8 applied to an unseen country context
Using the resource booklet to interpret unfamiliar information
Decision-making exercise: evaluating options and justifying a decision

topics.name: Topic 9 Geographical skills (assessed across all papers)
points: 9.1 Cartographic skills: maps, OS maps, cross sections, coordinates, scale, gradient, contours, GIS
9.2 Graphical skills: constructing, selecting and interpreting graphs and charts
9.3 Numerical and statistical skills: central tendency, spread, percentages, relationships, trend lines
9.4 Enquiry and argument: analysing images and written articles, evaluating sources
